name: Sign & wide-format print shops
hypothesis: Most run on spreadsheets + Shopify. Quote/estimate + production scheduling + proofing gap.

market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner/operator of a sign or wide-format print shop (typical 1–10 staff). Larger shops add a production/operations manager who becomes the primary user. ASGA reports the average member has ~$1M turnover and 5 staff.
market_sizing.business_count_au: 8,000–10,000 sign-industry businesses in Australia per ASGA, employing ~25,000 people, total industry turnover ~AU$4B. The wide-format/print-shop subset that does in-house production is roughly 4,000–6,000 shops; the remainder are installers, designers, or one-person operators.
market_sizing.business_count_global: Global TAM ~150,000–200,000 sign & wide-format shops. US has ~70,000+ (SGIA/PRINTING United Alliance reports); UK ~8,000; Canada ~6,000–8,000. EU adds tens of thousands more.
market_sizing.typical_size: 2–10 employees; AU$300K–$3M revenue. Mix of signwriting + wide-format printing + vehicle wraps + installation.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: shopVOX: Express US$99/mo + US$19/user; Pro US$199/mo + US$39/user — typical small AU shop lands at US$250–500/mo (~AU$400–800). Printavo: US$49–199/mo (Starter/Standard/Premium); customers report price hikes to ~US$399/mo after Inktavo/PSG buyout. FluidPSM (AU-built): AU$149/mo flat, unlimited users — undercuts everyone. Hexicom HexiHub: contact-sales, market reports AU$200–400/mo. ONYX Align: contact-sales, US$150–300/mo equivalent. Tradeprint/Coreprint: enterprise pricing.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AU sign shops pay AU$150–400/mo today (FluidPSM at AU$149 unlimited has set a low anchor). A premium AU-built entrant can reach AU$300–500/mo if it ships production scheduling + proofing + Xero/MYOB. ~75% of US ARPU is the realistic ceiling.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Self-serve trial + inside sales. Sign shops are tradeshow-driven (Visual Impact Sept 2026 Sydney, PacPrint Sydney 2025). Demos close most deals.
pricing_reality.realistic_arpu_au: AU$250–350/mo. AU$200 starter, AU$400 multi-user, AU$600+ for shops doing >AU$2M with installer crews.
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Strong 2–3× lever via embedded payments (deposit/progress invoices on AU$5K–50K signage jobs), supplier ordering (substrates, vinyl, banner from Ball & Doggett, Spicers, Avery Dennison), and a proofing/customer-portal feature monetised as a per-user upsell. AI-assisted quoting from spec sheets is another credible upsell.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) shopVOX (US, founded 2013) — most widely-used cross-vertical print/sign/embroidery tool, decent AU presence including 'largest sign maker in Perth' testimonial. 2) Printavo (US, now Inktavo/PSG, founded 2014) — strong screen-print roots, weaker for true wide-format/install workflow; price hikes generating churn signals. 3) FluidPSM (AU-built, AU$149/mo unlimited users) — local entrant, aggressive pricing, full quote→install→invoice with Xero/MYOB and a built-in AI helper. 4) HexiHub / Hexicom (AU contact +61 2 8005 1380) — established AU-relevant tool serving 1–20-user sign shops. 5) ONYX Align — RIP-adjacent quoting/scheduling, US-led. 6) Coreprint / Tharstern / EFI Pace — enterprise commercial print, too heavy. 7) SignTracker (Inktavo group) — legacy small sign-shop tool. 8) Nubium (Ball & Doggett, AU 2025 launch).
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: shopVOX ~13 years; Printavo ~12 years (rolled into Inktavo); SignTracker ~20 years (legacy); ONYX (parent ONYX Graphics) ~30 years; Hexicom ~15+ years. Most are 10–20 years old with dated UIs — solid replatform window.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: PrintPlanet and t-shirtforums threads on Printavo: 'famous for promising to fix functionality problems and then ignore them for literally YEARS', 'no read/write permissions', 'no customer overpayment feature', PE-driven price hikes from US$2,500/yr to US$3,990/yr after buyout. ShopVOX criticised for complexity and slow performance on Capterra. ONYX Align positions itself as 'replace spreadsheets with 4-click quoting' — implying the baseline is still spreadsheets. AU-specific complaint pattern: lack of MYOB support and US-centric tax/templates.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Major: Inktavo (Printavo + InkSoft + SignTracker + GraphicsFlow + Clarity, PSG/Blue Star-backed) merged with OrderMyGear in October 2025 — large branded-merch consolidation. Microvellum/INNERGY consolidation in adjacent millwork (Mar 2025). FluidPSM (AU) appears bootstrapped. Nubium (Ball & Doggett distributor-led) launched Apr 2025.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Medium. FluidPSM already ships an in-app AI helper. ONYX is layering AI on RIP/quoting. No fully AI-native pure-play has raised a public round in sign/wide-format yet, but the surface (auto-quote from artwork dimensions, AI proof generation) is highly attackable. 12–18 month window.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Three stacked pains: (1) Quoting consistency — every shop has a custom Excel pricing matrix per substrate/size/finish/install; estimators leave and the IP walks. (2) Proofing back-and-forth via email/WhatsApp with no audit trail (designs, change orders, sign-off). (3) Production scheduling across mixed equipment (large-format printer → laminator → cutter → CNC router → install crew) with shared bottleneck resources. Most shops still run on Shopify (web orders) + Xero (invoices) + Excel (quotes) + Trello/whiteboard (production), with no single source of truth.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Substrate/finish/install pricing rules engine; AU supplier integrations (Ball & Doggett, Spicers, Currie Group, IVE Group); proofing portal with audit trail; install scheduling with mobile sign-off. Defensibility = data (price templates), switching cost (pricing IP locked in), and AU compliance/payments.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Xero, MYOB AccountRight/Business; Stripe/Pinch/Tyro for AU payments; Ball & Doggett and Spicers supplier ordering APIs/EDI; Adobe Creative Cloud / artwork file handling; Onyx/Caldera RIP queues; Shopify (many shops have a B2B store); Google Maps for install routing; HubSpot/Pipedrive for sales.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: None equivalent to EHR. Most shops use loosely-coupled tools (Shopify + Xero + Excel + Trello). Rip-and-replace of the spreadsheet/whiteboard layer is the standard sale — not a side-car play.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Low. Australian Consumer Law (consumer-facing quotes/deposits), GST/Tax Invoice formatting, WHS for installers working at height. No licensing of the SaaS itself.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: Minor: NSW Engineered Stone Ban (national, 1 July 2024) — peripheral, only affects shops doing benchtop signage. NSW Modern Slavery & Federal Modern Slavery Act amendments tightening supply-chain reporting (substrate sourcing, ongoing 2025–2026). e-Invoicing (Peppol) mandate for Commonwealth agencies (already in force 2022 onward) plus state-level rollouts through 2025–2026 — shops doing govt/council signage will need e-invoicing-ready software. No single hard forcing function like NSW eCoC for electricians.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: Moderate. Need to understand substrates (ACM, corflute, foamboard, vinyl), print profiles (CMYK+W, white ink), lamination, cutting, installation site logistics, council permits for signage. Acquirable by an outsider in 3–6 months. Manuva's manufacturing ops mental model transfers cleanly.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 4–6 months for solo/small team to ship quoting + proofing + scheduling + Xero. Install scheduling and supplier ordering add 3–6 months.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: Pricing-rules engine flexibility (every shop's matrix is different); proofing portal large-file handling and version control; install scheduling with multi-resource constraints. No truly hard ML required for MVP.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: Minor. Council/local government signage permit rules differ by LGA, but the SaaS doesn't need to embed permit logic — links/templates are sufficient.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: None statutory. AU hosting (Supabase Sydney region) is a sales talking point especially for shops doing government/council work.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: (1) Visual Impact Conference & Expo 2026 (2–4 Sept, Sydney Olympic Park) — dominant AU sign/print event, alongside Connect Conference launching 2026. (2) PacPrint (biennial, Sydney 2025, Melbourne 2027) — covers commercial+sign+wide-format. (3) ASGA membership channel — newsletter, awards (next 3 Sept 2026 with Visual Impact). (4) Print21 magazine & email newsletter — primary AU trade publication, sponsorship AU$1–5K. (5) Wide Format Online (wideformatonline.com) news+newsletter. (6) Facebook groups for Australian sign-makers (multiple, ~5–15K combined). (7) Supplier co-marketing (Ball & Doggett's Nubium positioning suggests appetite). (8) Cold outbound: ASGA directory + ABN scrape gives ~8K targets.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 2 primary: ASGA (Australian Sign & Graphics Association) and Visual Connections (broader print/visual industry events). PIAA (Print Industries Association of Australia) is adjacent for commercial print.
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: 3–5: Print21, Wide Format Online, Sign Update (AU), Australian Printer, Image Magazine. All have paid sponsorship/newsletter slots.
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: ~5,000–10,000 combined across 'Sign Makers Australia', 'Wide Format Print Australia', and brand-specific groups. Smaller than cabinet/woodworking communities but engaged.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 2–3 main: Visual Impact (annual rotating Sydney/Melbourne), PacPrint (biennial), ASGA awards. Smaller state ASGA events. Booths AU$5–15K.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: High. Sign shops have public websites, ABN, and ASGA directory listings. Owner emails are findable. Quote requests are a natural front-door for outbound.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Moderate-high. Sign shop owners are trade-pragmatic and respond to clear ROI demos. Insider status not required; visiting 10 shops and shipping a credible quoting demo is enough to build trust. AU-built/AU-supported is a strong positioning lever vs US-headquartered shopVOX/Printavo.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Low-medium. 3–5 customers via direct ASGA outreach + one Visual Impact booth in 3–4 months. FluidPSM appears to have done this with limited budget.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Moderate. 'Sign shop management software Australia' is winnable; long-tail ('wide format quoting AU', 'sign proofing portal') is wide open. Head terms dominated by shopVOX, Printavo.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: None. No gatekeeper API. Shopify/Xero/MYOB/Stripe are all open APIs accessible to startups.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: 45–55%. Inventory (substrates, vinyl rolls, hardware), suppliers, purchase orders, production orders, locations, activity log all reuse. New domain: pricing-rules engine (size × substrate × finish × install), proofing/file-versioning, install scheduling with mobile sign-off. BOM concept maps loosely but is less central than in cabinet/manufacturing.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Auth, tenant context, RLS, activity_log, Xero/MYOB sync skeleton, supplier/PO/inventory UI, dashboards reusable. Proofing portal and mobile install app are new builds.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Low-medium. Sign shops are a different buyer (graphic/trade-services mix) than Manuva's discrete-manufacturer ICP. Some overlap with shops that also do signage manufacturing (CNC routing of letters, fabricated signs), but largely a fresh GTM.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Medium. Production scheduling and supplier/inventory concepts transfer; the front-office (quoting, proofing) is a different muscle than Manuva's current focus.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 6–12 months. The 'pricing engine + proofing + scheduling + Xero' bundle is reproducible by an AI-tooled competitor in under a year. FluidPSM already exists at AU$149 unlimited — moat must come from depth (supplier integrations, install workflow, payments) not surface.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy 80%+ GM achievable. Proofing portals consume storage (large artwork files at 300dpi) — 50–500GB per shop — but Supabase Storage/R2 keeps this <2% of ARPU. AI proof/quote features add small inference cost. No SMS-heavy workflows.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Moderate. Larger shops grow to 2–3 production sites and separate install depots; some chains exist (Signarama, Kwik Kopy, Snap). Multi-location is a real expansion path but not the dominant pattern.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Moderate. Sign shops are project-driven and small; ~10–15% annual SMB churn is typical. Failure mode: shop closes (housing/retail slowdown) rather than competitor switch.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: ~280–330 customers at AU$300/mo ARPU for AU$1M ARR. ~5% AU sign-shop share. Realistic in 3 years with focused GTM, harder if FluidPSM continues at AU$149.
